data.name: AdmThemesGuideSeed
data.value: From one colour: pick a seed and a harmony and press Generate. This runs MarkupString's ThemePalette.Generate, the same generator the game's layout themes use. The harmony picks the other hues: monochrome keeps the seed's, analogous takes its neighbours, complementary its opposite, split the two either side of the opposite, triadic and tetradic three or four evenly round the wheel. Contrast raises every colour from the minimum (4.5:1 for text) toward 7:1.

data.name: AdmThemesGuidePreset
data.value: From a palette: the presets are ThemePalette.Presets. The eight genre palettes (fantasy, horror, science-fiction...) are generated, so they are made again for this theme's light or dark mode. The base16 schemes (nord, dracula, solarized-dark...) are fixed colours and bring their own mode with them.

data.name: AdmThemesGuideJson
data.value: From JSON: paste what layout_theme and a layout function's theme option take. That is a preset's name; an object with seed, harmony, contrast and mode; an object with base16 (sixteen colours); or any of those with colors setting roles (background, surface, foreground, primary, warning, error...).

data.name: AdmThemesGuideMapping
data.value: How a palette becomes a theme: its background is the page and its surface the cards, its foreground the text, with the dim and faint text mixed toward the page. Its primary is the accent, its warning the warning colour and its error the missing-link colour. Each text colour is then moved toward white or black until it reads at 4.5:1 on every surface, so a generated theme passes the contrast report.
